source.text: Καὶ ἦλθον εἰς τὸ πέραν τῆς θαλάσσης εἰς τὴν χώραν τῶν Γερασηνῶν.

records.literal_gloss: And they came to the other side of the sea, to the region of the Gerasenes.

en.L: And they came to the other side of the sea, to the region of the Gerasenes.
en.B: They reached the far side of the lake, the country of the Gerasenes.
en.R: Jesus and {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} followers crossed Lake Galilee to the other side. They came to the land where the Gerasene people lived.

es.L: Y llegaron al otro lado del mar, a la región de los gerasenos.
es.B: Llegaron a la otra orilla del lago, a la tierra de los gerasenos.
es.R: Jesús y {{deity_pronoun:sus|Sus}} discípulos cruzaron el lago de Galilea hasta la otra orilla. Llegaron a la tierra donde vivían los gerasenos.

sw.L: Na wakafika ng'ambo ya pili ya bahari, katika nchi ya Wagerasi.
sw.B: Walifika ng'ambo ya ziwa, katika nchi ya Wagerasi.
sw.R: Yesu na wanafunzi {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}} walivuka Ziwa Galilaya hadi upande wa pili. Wakafika katika nchi walimoishi Wagerasi.

decisions.choice: Gerasenes, as the SBLGNT reads
decisions.reason: Manuscripts differ on the name. The earliest Alexandrian and Western witnesses have Gerasenes; many later manuscripts have Gadarenes, the name in Matthew 8:28; some have Gergesenes. Gerasa and Gadara were towns of the Decapolis some distance from the lake, and the name may refer to the wider district rather than the town itself. Reviewers should check this against the SBLGNT apparatus.

decisions.choice: the other side of the sea: the eastern shore of the Sea of Galilee
decisions.reason: The crossing began in 4:35. The eastern shore was mostly Gentile country, which explains the herd of pigs (5:11).

decisions.choice: they came: Jesus and his disciples, who set out in 4:35-36
decisions.reason: The plural carries on from the storm on the lake. From 5:2 Mark follows Jesus alone.

decisions.choice: Jesus and his followers crossed Lake Galilee
alternatives: they came to the other side of the sea
decisions.reason: Readable names who is travelling and which lake it is.

decisions.choice: el mar (L); el lago (B); el lago de Galilea (R)
decisions.reason: As the term sheet settles and as in Matthew 13:1: the "sea" is the Sea of Galilee, a freshwater lake (meaning decision m2). Literal keeps "mar", the Greek word; Balanced and Readable say "lago". The same in verses 13 and 21.

decisions.choice: discípulos at every level
decisions.reason: Where the English Readable says "followers", Spanish keeps "discípulos", a common word every reader knows, as the term sheet settles for the whole New Testament. The same through the chapter (verses 31, 40 and 42).

decisions.choice: bahari (L); ziwa (B); Ziwa Galilaya (R)
decisions.reason: Swahili "bahari" is the open sea; the Sea of Galilee is a freshwater lake (meaning decision m2), which Swahili calls "ziwa", as in Ziwa Viktoria. Literal keeps "bahari", the word of the Greek. The same in verses 13 and 21.

decisions.choice: wanafunzi at every level
decisions.reason: Where the English Readable says "followers", Swahili keeps "wanafunzi", the everyday word for a teacher's disciples, as the term sheet settles. The same through the chapter (verses 31, 40 and 42).

source.text: καὶ ἐξελθόντος αὐτοῦ ἐκ τοῦ πλοίου εὐθὺς ὑπήντησεν αὐτῷ ἐκ τῶν μνημείων ἄνθρωπος ἐν πνεύματι ἀκαθάρτῳ, ὃς τὴν κατοίκησιν εἶχεν ἐν τοῖς μνήμασιν, καὶ οὐδὲ ἁλύσει οὐκέτι οὐδεὶς ἐδύνατο αὐτὸν δῆσαι διὰ τὸ αὐτὸν πολλάκις πέδαις καὶ ἁλύσεσι δεδέσθαι καὶ διεσπάσθαι ὑπ’ αὐτοῦ τὰς ἁλύσεις καὶ τὰς πέδας συντετρῖφθαι, καὶ οὐδεὶς ἴσχυεν αὐτὸν δαμάσαι·

records.literal_gloss: And having gone out of him out of the boat, immediately met him out of the tombs a man with a spirit unclean, \v 3 who the dwelling had in the tombs, and not even with a chain no longer anyone was able him to bind, \v 4 because him often with shackles and chains to have been bound, and to have been torn apart by him the chains and the shackles to have been shattered, and no one was strong enough him to subdue.

en.L: And when {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} had come out of the boat, immediately a man with an unclean spirit met {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} [coming] out of the tombs, \v 3 who had his dwelling among the tombs, and no one was able any longer to bind him, not even with a chain, \v 4 because he had often been bound with shackles and chains, and the chains had been torn apart by him and the shackles shattered, and no one was strong enough to subdue him.
en.B: As soon as {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} stepped out of the boat, a man with an unclean spirit came out from the tombs to meet {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}. \v 3 This man lived among the tombs, and nobody could keep him tied up anymore, not even with a chain. \v 4 Time and again he had been bound hand and foot with irons and chains, but he had pulled the chains apart and smashed the irons on his feet. No one had the strength to control him.
en.R: Jesus got out of the boat. Right away a man came out from the burial caves to meet {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}. The man had an evil spirit in him. \v 3 He lived in the burial caves. No one could tie him up anymore, not even with chains. \v 4 People had often put chains on his hands and feet. But he always broke the chains apart and smashed the metal rings on his feet. No one was strong enough to control him.

es.L: Y cuando {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} salió de la barca, en seguida {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} salió al encuentro, [viniendo] de los sepulcros, un hombre con un espíritu impuro, \v 3 que tenía su morada entre los sepulcros, y nadie podía ya atarlo, ni siquiera con una cadena, \v 4 porque muchas veces había sido atado con grilletes y cadenas, y las cadenas habían sido despedazadas por él y los grilletes hechos añicos, y nadie tenía fuerza para domarlo.
es.B: En cuanto bajó de la barca, un hombre con un espíritu impuro salió de entre los sepulcros a {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} encuentro. \v 3 Este hombre vivía entre los sepulcros, y ya nadie podía tenerlo atado, ni siquiera con cadenas. \v 4 Muchas veces le habían sujetado los pies con grilletes y lo habían atado con cadenas, pero él había hecho pedazos las cadenas y había roto los grilletes. Nadie tenía fuerza para dominarlo.
es.R: Jesús bajó de la barca. En seguida un hombre salió de las cuevas donde se enterraba a los muertos y fue a {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} encuentro. Ese hombre tenía dentro un espíritu maligno. \v 3 Vivía en las cuevas de los muertos. Ya nadie podía atarlo, ni siquiera con cadenas. \v 4 Muchas veces le habían puesto cadenas en las manos y en los pies. Pero él siempre rompía las cadenas y hacía pedazos los aros de hierro de sus pies. Nadie tenía fuerza para controlarlo.

sw.L: Na alipotoka katika mashua, mara mtu mwenye pepo mchafu kutoka makaburini akakutana {{deity_pronoun:naye|Naye}}, \v 3 ambaye makao yake yalikuwa makaburini, wala hakuna mtu aliyeweza tena kumfunga, hata kwa mnyororo, \v 4 kwa sababu mara nyingi alikuwa amefungwa kwa pingu na minyororo, naye alikuwa ameikatakata minyororo na kuzivunjavunja pingu, wala hakuna mtu aliyekuwa na nguvu za kumfuga.
sw.B: Mara tu alipotoka katika mashua, mtu mwenye pepo mchafu alitoka makaburini, akaja kukutana {{deity_pronoun:naye|Naye}}. \v 3 Mtu huyo aliishi makaburini, na hakuna mtu aliyeweza tena kumfunga, hata kwa minyororo. \v 4 Mara nyingi alikuwa amefungwa miguu kwa pingu na kufungwa kwa minyororo, lakini aliikatakata minyororo na kuzivunjavunja pingu. Hakuna mtu aliyekuwa na nguvu za kumdhibiti.
sw.R: Yesu alishuka kutoka kwenye mashua. Mara mtu mmoja alitoka kwenye mapango ya kuzikia wafu, akaja kukutana {{deity_pronoun:naye|Naye}}. Mtu huyo alikuwa na pepo mbaya ndani yake. \v 3 Aliishi katika mapango hayo ya kuzikia. Hakuna mtu aliyeweza kumfunga tena, hata kwa minyororo. \v 4 Mara nyingi watu walikuwa wamemfunga minyororo mikononi na miguuni. Lakini kila mara aliikata minyororo hiyo na kuvunja pete za chuma za miguu yake. Hakuna mtu aliyekuwa na nguvu za kumzuia.

decisions.choice: the tombs: burial caves cut in the hillside
decisions.reason: Tombs in that region were often caves or rooms cut into rock, where a person could shelter. To live among the dead made a person unclean in Jewish law (Numbers 19:11-16).

decisions.choice: not even with a chain, no longer, no one: a string of negatives for emphasis
alternatives: a weaker statement that binding was hard
decisions.reason: Greek piles up negatives to make the point stronger: nothing at all could hold him any more.

decisions.choice: shackles: fetters for the feet
decisions.reason: The word is used for chains or irons on the feet, set beside chains, which could bind the hands.

decisions.choice: subdue: tame, as one tames a wild animal
decisions.reason: The verb is used for taming animals (James 3:7). The man is pictured as wild and beyond human control.

decisions.choice: burial caves
decisions.reason: Readable says what kind of tombs a man could live in.

decisions.choice: the long clause is split into separate sentences
alternatives: one sentence with a chain of infinitives
decisions.reason: Balanced breaks the sentence where the Greek gives the reason, to keep it readable.

decisions.choice: espíritu impuro (L, B); espíritu maligno (R)
decisions.reason: The term used across the New Testament drafts, as in Matthew 10:1. "Inmundo" now sounds like dirt; "impuro" says the spirit makes a person unfit to come near God, and Readable says plainly that it is evil, as the English does. The same through the chapter.

decisions.choice: sepulcros (L, B); las cuevas donde se enterraba a los muertos (R)
decisions.reason: The term sheet has "tumba" at Readable, but these were burial caves cut in the hillside (meaning decision m1), and the English Readable says so, as in Matthew 8:28. The same in verse 5.

decisions.choice: pepo mchafu (L, B); pepo mbaya (R)
decisions.reason: The term used across the New Testament drafts for an unclean spirit, which is a demon, as in Matthew 10:1. "Roho" is kept for the human spirit and the Spirit of God. Readable says plainly that the spirit is evil, as the English does. The same through the chapter.

decisions.choice: kumfuga (L); kumdhibiti (B); kumzuia (R)
decisions.reason: The verb is used for taming a wild animal (meaning decision m4). "Kufuga" is to tame or keep animals, so Literal keeps the picture; Balanced and Readable say "control", as the English does.

source.text: καὶ διὰ παντὸς νυκτὸς καὶ ἡμέρας ἐν τοῖς μνήμασιν καὶ ἐν τοῖς ὄρεσιν ἦν κράζων καὶ κατακόπτων ἑαυτὸν λίθοις.

records.literal_gloss: And constantly night and day in the tombs and in the mountains he was crying out and cutting himself with stones.

en.L: And constantly, night and day, among the tombs and in the mountains he was crying out and cutting himself with stones.
en.B: Night and day, without stopping, he would scream among the tombs and on the hills and slash himself with stones.
en.R: All night and all day he was in the burial caves and in the hills. He kept screaming and cutting himself with sharp stones.

es.L: Y continuamente, noche y día, entre los sepulcros y en los montes, estaba gritando e hiriéndose con piedras.
es.B: Noche y día, sin parar, andaba gritando entre los sepulcros y por los cerros, y se hacía cortes con piedras.
es.R: Pasaba toda la noche y todo el día en las cuevas de los muertos y en los cerros. Gritaba sin parar y se cortaba con piedras afiladas.

sw.L: Na daima, usiku na mchana, makaburini na milimani, alikuwa akipiga kelele na kujikatakata kwa mawe.
sw.B: Usiku na mchana, bila kukoma, alikuwa akipiga makelele makaburini na vilimani, na kujikatakata kwa mawe.
sw.R: Usiku wote na mchana wote alikuwa katika mapango ya kuzikia na vilimani. Aliendelea kupiga kelele na kujikata kwa mawe makali.

decisions.choice: he was crying out and cutting: an ongoing state
decisions.reason: The verb with participles describes what he kept doing, day after day.

decisions.choice: cutting: gashing, wounding
decisions.reason: The verb means to cut or gash. The spirit drives the man to harm himself.

decisions.choice: the mountains: the hills around the lake
decisions.reason: The word covers hill country as well as high mountains.

source.text: καὶ ἰδὼν τὸν Ἰησοῦν ἀπὸ μακρόθεν ἔδραμεν καὶ προσεκύνησεν αὐτόν, καὶ κράξας φωνῇ μεγάλῃ λέγει· Τί ἐμοὶ καὶ σοί, Ἰησοῦ υἱὲ τοῦ θεοῦ τοῦ ὑψίστου;

records.literal_gloss: And having seen the Jesus from afar, he ran and bowed down to him, \v 7 and having cried out with a voice loud, he says, What to me and to you, Jesus, Son of the God the Most High?

en.L: And seeing Jesus from a distance, he ran and bowed down before {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, \v 7 and crying out with a loud voice, he says, "What [is there] to me and to {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}, Jesus, Son of the Most High God?
en.B: When he caught sight of Jesus a long way off, he ran up and threw himself down in front of {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}. \v 7 He gave a loud shriek: "Jesus, Son of the Most High God, what have {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} to do with me?
en.R: The man saw Jesus far away. He ran to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} and got down on his knees in front of {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}. \v 7 He shouted very loudly, "Jesus, Son of the Most High God, why are {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} bothering me?

es.L: Y viendo a Jesús desde lejos, corrió y se postró ante {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}}, \v 7 y gritando con gran voz, dice: «¿Qué [hay] para mí y para {{deity_pronoun:ti|Ti}}, Jesús, Hijo del Dios Altísimo?
es.B: Cuando vio a Jesús desde lejos, corrió y se postró delante de {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}}. \v 7 Dio un alarido: «Jesús, Hijo del Dios Altísimo, ¿qué tienes que ver conmigo?
es.R: El hombre vio a Jesús desde lejos. Corrió hacia {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} y se arrodilló delante de {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}}. \v 7 Gritó muy fuerte: «Jesús, Hijo del Dios Altísimo, ¿por qué me molestas?

sw.L: Na alipomwona Yesu kwa mbali, alikimbia, akamsujudia, \v 7 na akipiga kelele kwa sauti kuu, anasema, "Kuna nini kati yangu na {{deity_pronoun:wewe|Wewe}}, Yesu, Mwana wa Mungu Aliye Juu Kabisa?
sw.B: Alipomwona Yesu kwa mbali, alikimbia, akajitupa chini mbele {{deity_pronoun:yake|Yake}}. \v 7 Akapiga kelele kwa sauti kubwa, "Yesu, Mwana wa Mungu Aliye Juu Kabisa, una shughuli gani nami?
sw.R: Yule mtu alimwona Yesu akiwa mbali. Alikimbia {{deity_pronoun:kwake|Kwake}}, akapiga magoti mbele {{deity_pronoun:yake|Yake}}. \v 7 Akapiga kelele kwa sauti kubwa sana, "Yesu, Mwana wa Mungu Aliye Juu Kabisa, kwa nini unanisumbua?

decisions.choice: bowed down: fell to his knees in homage
decisions.reason: The verb is used for kneeling before a king or a god. Here the spirit is forced to bow before one stronger than itself (3:11), not to trust in him.

decisions.choice: what to me and to you: what do we have in common? leave me alone
decisions.reason: As in 1:24, the phrase keeps someone at a distance and is hostile here.

decisions.choice: Son of the Most High God: the spirit knows who Jesus is
alternatives: a title the man had heard from others
decisions.reason: "Most High" is an old name for the God of Israel (Genesis 14:18-20) used also by non-Jews (Acts 16:17). The unclean spirits know Jesus as the Son of God (1:24; 3:11).

decisions.choice: he says: the present tense of storytelling
decisions.reason: Mark often tells past events in the present tense to make them vivid. The same is true of the presents through this chapter.

decisions.choice: said, shouted
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable use the past tense, which English uses for telling a story.

decisions.choice: why are you bothering me?
alternatives: what to me and to you?
decisions.reason: Readable gives the sense of the idiom.

decisions.choice: historic present at Literal (dice); pretérito at Balanced and Readable (dio un alarido, gritó)
decisions.reason: Mark tells much of this chapter in the present (meaning decision m4). Literal keeps it, as the English Literal does; Balanced and Readable tell the story in the past, as Spanish narrative does. The same in verses 9, 15, 19, 22-23, 35-36 and 38-41.

decisions.choice: ¿Qué [hay] para mí y para ti?
decisions.reason: The Greek idiom says "what to me and to you" (meaning decision m2). Literal keeps its two datives in their order, so the separate pronoun "ti" can carry the setting; Balanced and Readable say what it means.

decisions.choice: historic present kept at Literal (anasema); past at Balanced and Readable (akapiga kelele)
decisions.reason: Mark tells much of this chapter in the present (meaning decision m4). Literal keeps it, as the English Literal does; Balanced and Readable tell the story in the narrative past, with -li- for the first verb and -ka- for those that follow. The same in verses 9, 15, 19, 22-23, 35-36 and 38-41.

decisions.choice: Mungu Aliye Juu Kabisa
decisions.reason: The Greek is a superlative, "the Highest". "Aliye Juu Kabisa" (who is highest of all) says that, as in Hebrews 7:1.

source.text: ὁρκίζω σε τὸν θεόν, μή με βασανίσῃς.

records.literal_gloss: I adjure you by the God, not me torment.

en.L: I adjure {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} by God, do not torment me!"
en.B: I beg {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}, with God as witness, do not torture me!"
en.R: Promise me in God's name that {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} will not hurt me!"

es.L: Te conjuro por Dios: ¡no me atormentes!».
es.B: Con Dios por testigo {{deity_pronoun:te|Te}} suplico: ¡no me tortures!».
es.R: ¡Prométeme por Dios que no me vas a hacer daño!».

sw.L: Nakuapisha kwa Mungu, usinitese!"
sw.B: Nakusihi, Mungu akiwa shahidi, usinitese!"
sw.R: Niahidi kwa jina la Mungu kwamba hutaniumiza!"

decisions.choice: I adjure you: I put you under oath
decisions.reason: The verb means to make someone swear by God. It is the language used to drive out spirits, here turned against Jesus.

decisions.choice: torment: punish, torture
decisions.reason: The spirits expect punishment at the judgment (Matthew 8:29). The verb is used for torture and for punishment.

decisions.choice: I beg you, with God as witness (B); Promise me in God's name (R)
decisions.reason: "Adjure" is rare in modern English. Balanced and Readable say what the oath formula means.

decisions.choice: deity_pronoun spans only on separate pronouns and possessives: te (B); none at Literal and Readable
alternatives: a span on every pronoun the English marks
decisions.reason: Spanish usually leaves the subject pronoun out ("vas") and joins some object pronouns to the verb ("prométeme"), and a pronoun that begins the sentence ("Te conjuro") is capitalised in any case, so there is nothing for the setting to change. The setting therefore covers fewer words than in English. This holds for the whole chapter.

decisions.choice: te conjuro (L); te suplico (B); prométeme (R)
decisions.reason: The verb puts someone under oath (meaning decision m1). "Conjurar" keeps that solemn sense at Literal; Balanced and Readable say it with an appeal to God as witness and a request for a promise, as the English does.

decisions.choice: no deity_pronoun span on nakuapisha, nakusihi (I adjure you, I beg you)
decisions.reason: The English "you" takes the setting. Swahili carries it in the object prefix -ku- of the verb, which cannot take a capital, so the setting applies only to free pronouns and possessives (naye, wewe, yake), as in John and Matthew. Swahili therefore has fewer spans than English throughout the chapter.

decisions.choice: nakuapisha (L); nakusihi (B); niahidi (R)
decisions.reason: The verb puts someone under oath (meaning decision m1). "Kuapisha" (to make someone swear) keeps that at Literal; Balanced and Readable say it as a plea with God as witness and a request for a promise, as the English does.

source.text: ἔλεγεν γὰρ αὐτῷ· Ἔξελθε τὸ πνεῦμα τὸ ἀκάθαρτον ἐκ τοῦ ἀνθρώπου.

records.literal_gloss: He was saying for to him, Come out, the spirit the unclean, out of the man.

en.L: For {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} had been saying to him, "Come out of the man, unclean spirit!"
en.B: This was because Jesus had been telling it, "Unclean spirit, come out of this man!"
en.R: The man said this because Jesus was already telling the evil spirit, "Get out of this man, evil spirit!"

es.L: Porque {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} le decía: «¡Sal del hombre, espíritu impuro!».
es.B: Es que Jesús le estaba diciendo: «¡Espíritu impuro, sal de este hombre!».
es.R: El hombre dijo eso porque Jesús ya le estaba ordenando al espíritu maligno: «¡Sal de este hombre, espíritu maligno!».

sw.L: Kwa maana {{deity_pronoun:yeye|Yeye}} alikuwa akimwambia, "Toka ndani ya mtu huyu, wewe pepo mchafu!"
sw.B: Hii ni kwa sababu Yesu alikuwa akimwambia, "Pepo mchafu, mtoke mtu huyu!"
sw.R: Mtu huyo alisema hivyo kwa sababu Yesu alikuwa tayari akimwamuru yule pepo mbaya, "Toka ndani ya mtu huyu, wewe pepo mbaya!"

decisions.choice: for he had been saying: the reason for the spirit's outcry
decisions.reason: Mark explains afterwards what had already happened. The verb can mean that Jesus had begun to command it, or was commanding it while the spirit cried out.

decisions.choice: the unclean spirit: Jesus speaks to the spirit, not the man
alternatives: the man is told to leave
decisions.reason: The words are addressed to the spirit, which is to leave the man.

decisions.choice: This was because (B); The man said this because (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable spell out what "for" explains.

source.text: καὶ ἐπηρώτα αὐτόν· Τί ὄνομά σοι;

records.literal_gloss: And he was asking him, What name to you?

en.L: And {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} was asking him, "What [is] your name?"
en.B: Then Jesus asked him, "What is your name?"
en.R: Then Jesus asked, "What is your name?"

es.L: Y {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} le preguntaba: «¿Cuál [es] tu nombre?».
es.B: Entonces Jesús le preguntó: «¿Cómo te llamas?».
es.R: Entonces Jesús le preguntó: «¿Cómo te llamas?».

sw.L: Naye akamwuliza, "Jina lako [ni] nani?"
sw.B: Kisha Yesu alimwuliza, "Jina lako ni nani?"
sw.R: Kisha Yesu akauliza, "Unaitwa nani?"

decisions.choice: him, your: addressed to the man, but the spirit answers
decisions.reason: The reply in 5:9 shows the spirits speaking through him.

decisions.choice: what is your name: knowing a spirit's name was thought to give power over it
decisions.reason: Jesus does not need a name to drive out spirits, but the answer shows how many hold the man.

source.text: καὶ λέγει αὐτῷ· Λεγιὼν ὄνομά μοι, ὅτι πολλοί ἐσμεν·

records.literal_gloss: And he says to him, Legion name to me, because many we are.

en.L: And he says to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, "Legion [is] my name, because we are many."
en.B: He answered, "My name is Legion, since there are many of us."
en.R: He answered, "My name is Legion, because there are so many of us."

es.L: Y {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} dice: «Legión [es] mi nombre, porque somos muchos».
es.B: Respondió: «Me llamo Legión, porque somos muchos».
es.R: Contestó: «Me llamo Legión, porque somos muchísimos».

sw.L: Naye anamwambia, "Jina langu [ni] Legioni, kwa kuwa tu wengi."
sw.B: Akajibu, "Jina langu ni Legioni, kwa maana tuko wengi."
sw.R: Akajibu, "Naitwa Legioni, kwa sababu sisi ni wengi sana."

decisions.choice: Legion: a Roman army unit of several thousand soldiers
alternatives: a vague word for a crowd
decisions.reason: A Roman legion had about 6,000 soldiers. The name says that a great many spirits hold the man, like an occupying army.

decisions.choice: my name ... we are many: the speaker shifts from one to many
decisions.reason: One voice speaks for many spirits. Mark keeps both singular and plural (5:10, 12).

decisions.choice: answered
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable use the past tense and leave the pronoun out.

decisions.choice: Legioni
decisions.reason: Legion is used as a name, taken from the Roman army unit of several thousand soldiers (meaning decision m1). "Jeshi" (army) would turn the name into an ordinary word; "Legioni" keeps it a name, and the meaning note says what it was. The same in verse 15.

source.text: καὶ παρεκάλει αὐτὸν πολλὰ ἵνα μὴ αὐτὰ ἀποστείλῃ ἔξω τῆς χώρας.

records.literal_gloss: And he was begging him much that not them he would send out of the region.

en.L: And he begged {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} many times not to send them out of the region.
en.B: He kept pleading with Jesus not to send them away out of that country.
en.R: He begged Jesus again and again, "Do not send us away from this area!"

es.L: Y {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} rogaba mucho que no los enviara fuera de la región.
es.B: Y suplicaba a Jesús una y otra vez que no los expulsara de aquella región.
es.R: Le rogaba a Jesús una y otra vez: «¡No nos eches de esta zona!».

sw.L: Naye akamsihi sana asiwapeleke nje ya nchi ile.
sw.B: Akaendelea kumsihi Yesu asiwafukuze kutoka katika nchi ile.
sw.R: Alimsihi Yesu tena na tena, "Usitufukuze kutoka eneo hili!"

decisions.choice: them: the spirits, though the man speaks
decisions.reason: The plural refers to the spirits, who speak through one voice.

decisions.choice: out of the region: away from the land where they dwelt
decisions.reason: Mark speaks of the region; Luke 8:31 has the abyss. The spirits want to stay where they are.

decisions.choice: direct speech: Do not send us away from this area!
alternatives: that he would not send them out of the region
decisions.reason: Readable turns the request into direct speech, which is easier to follow.

source.text: ἦν δὲ ἐκεῖ πρὸς τῷ ὄρει ἀγέλη χοίρων μεγάλη βοσκομένη·

records.literal_gloss: There was now there near the mountain a herd of pigs great feeding.

en.L: Now there was there near the mountain a great herd of pigs feeding.
en.B: A large herd of pigs happened to be grazing on the hillside nearby.
en.R: There was a big group of pigs eating on the hill close by.

es.L: Y había allí, junto al monte, una gran piara de cerdos paciendo.
es.B: Cerca de allí, en la ladera del monte, estaba paciendo una gran piara de cerdos.
es.R: En la colina cercana había una gran manada de cerdos comiendo.

sw.L: Basi palikuwa pale karibu na mlima kundi kubwa la nguruwe likila malisho.
sw.B: Kulikuwa na kundi kubwa la nguruwe likila malisho kwenye mteremko wa kilima karibu na pale.
sw.R: Kwenye kilima kilichokuwa karibu, kundi kubwa la nguruwe lilikuwa likila.

decisions.choice: a herd of pigs: animals the law of Moses calls unclean
alternatives: farm animals of no special meaning
decisions.reason: Jews did not eat or keep pigs (Leviticus 11:7). A large herd shows that this was Gentile country.

decisions.choice: near the mountain: on the slope of the hill
alternatives: at the foot of a high mountain
decisions.reason: The herd is on the hillside above the lake, from which it rushes down (5:13).

source.text: καὶ παρεκάλεσαν αὐτὸν λέγοντες· Πέμψον ἡμᾶς εἰς τοὺς χοίρους, ἵνα εἰς αὐτοὺς εἰσέλθωμεν.

records.literal_gloss: And they begged him saying, Send us into the pigs, so that into them we may enter.

en.L: And they begged {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, saying, "Send us into the pigs, so that we may enter into them."
en.B: The spirits pleaded with {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, "Send us over to the pigs. Let us go into them."
en.R: The evil spirits begged Jesus, "Let us go into the pigs! Send us into them!"

es.L: Y {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} rogaron, diciendo: «Envíanos a los cerdos, para que entremos en ellos».
es.B: Los espíritus {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} suplicaron: «Mándanos a los cerdos; déjanos entrar en ellos».
es.R: Los espíritus malignos le rogaron a Jesús: «¡Déjanos entrar en los cerdos! ¡Mándanos a ellos!».

sw.L: Nao wakamsihi, wakisema, "Tupeleke kwa nguruwe, ili tuwaingie."
sw.B: Pepo hao walimsihi, "Tupeleke kwa nguruwe. Turuhusu tuwaingie."
sw.R: Wale pepo wabaya walimsihi Yesu, "Turuhusu tuwaingie nguruwe! Tupeleke ndani yao!"

decisions.choice: they begged: the spirits, now in the plural
decisions.reason: The subject changes to the many spirits, who are named in 5:13.

decisions.choice: they begged him: without a named subject
decisions.reason: Many later manuscripts add a subject, "all the demons". The shorter text, which the SBLGNT prints, is found in the earliest witnesses. Reviewers should check this against the SBLGNT apparatus.

decisions.choice: the spirits (B); the evil spirits (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable name the subject, since "they" could mean the people.

source.text: καὶ ἐπέτρεψεν αὐτοῖς.

records.literal_gloss: And he permitted them.

en.L: And {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} permitted them.
en.B: He gave them leave.
en.R: Jesus let them go.

es.L: Y se lo permitió.
es.B: Y les dio permiso.
es.R: Jesús los dejó ir.

sw.L: Naye akawaruhusu.
sw.B: Akawapa ruhusa.
sw.R: Yesu aliwaruhusu waende.

decisions.choice: he permitted: the spirits can act only with Jesus' leave
decisions.reason: The spirits ask; Jesus decides. Mark shows his authority over them (1:27).

source.text: καὶ ἐξελθόντα τὰ πνεύματα τὰ ἀκάθαρτα εἰσῆλθον εἰς τοὺς χοίρους, καὶ ὥρμησεν ἡ ἀγέλη κατὰ τοῦ κρημνοῦ εἰς τὴν θάλασσαν, ὡς δισχίλιοι, καὶ ἐπνίγοντο ἐν τῇ θαλάσσῃ.

records.literal_gloss: And having gone out, the spirits the unclean entered into the pigs, and rushed the herd down the steep bank into the sea, about two thousand, and they were drowning in the sea.

en.L: And coming out, the unclean spirits entered into the pigs, and the herd rushed down the steep bank into the sea, about 2,000 [of them], and they were drowned in the sea.
en.B: Out came the unclean spirits, and they went into the pigs. The whole herd, about 2,000 animals, stampeded down the steep slope into the lake and drowned there.
en.R: The evil spirits left the man and went into the pigs. Then the pigs ran wildly down the steep hill into the lake. There were about 2,000 pigs, and all of them drowned in the water.

es.L: Y saliendo, los espíritus impuros entraron en los cerdos, y la piara se lanzó por el despeñadero al mar, unos dos mil, y se ahogaban en el mar.
es.B: Los espíritus impuros salieron y entraron en los cerdos. Toda la piara, unos dos mil animales, se precipitó cuesta abajo hacia el lago y allí se ahogó.
es.R: Los espíritus malignos salieron del hombre y entraron en los cerdos. Entonces los cerdos corrieron como locos por la ladera empinada hasta el lago. Eran unos dos mil cerdos, y todos se ahogaron en el agua.

sw.L: Na wale pepo wachafu wakitoka, wakaingia ndani ya nguruwe, na kundi likatimua mbio kuteremka genge kuingia baharini, kama elfu mbili, nao walikuwa wakizama baharini.
sw.B: Pepo wachafu walitoka, wakawaingia nguruwe. Kundi zima, nguruwe wapata elfu mbili, likatimua mbio kuteremka mteremko mkali hadi ziwani, likazama humo.
sw.R: Pepo wabaya walimtoka yule mtu, wakawaingia nguruwe. Kisha nguruwe wakakimbia kwa kasi kuteremka kilima kikali hadi ziwani. Walikuwa nguruwe kama elfu mbili, na wote wakazama majini.

decisions.choice: about two thousand: the size of the herd
decisions.reason: The number goes with the herd, and is the only number of animals Mark gives. It shows how many spirits had held the man.

decisions.choice: rushed: charged headlong
decisions.reason: The verb is used for a sudden violent rush.

decisions.choice: the spirits destroy what they enter
alternatives: Jesus wanted the pigs to drown
decisions.reason: What the spirits did to the pigs shows what they were doing to the man. The sea in Mark is also a place of chaos that Jesus rules (4:39-41).

decisions.choice: the lake
decisions.reason: As elsewhere, Balanced and Readable call the Sea of Galilee a lake, which it is.

source.text: Καὶ οἱ βόσκοντες αὐτοὺς ἔφυγον καὶ ἀπήγγειλαν εἰς τὴν πόλιν καὶ εἰς τοὺς ἀγρούς· καὶ ἦλθον ἰδεῖν τί ἐστιν τὸ γεγονός.

records.literal_gloss: And those feeding them fled and reported [it] in the city and in the fields; and they came to see what it is that has happened.

en.L: And those feeding them fled and reported [it] in the city and in the countryside, and [people] came to see what it was that had happened.
en.B: The men tending the pigs ran off and spread the news in the town and on the farms, and people came out to see what had taken place.
en.R: The men who took care of the pigs ran away. They told everyone in the town and on the farms what had happened. So people came out to see for themselves.

es.L: Y los que los apacentaban huyeron y [lo] contaron en la ciudad y en los campos; y vinieron a ver qué era lo que había sucedido.
es.B: Los que cuidaban los cerdos salieron corriendo y dieron la noticia en el pueblo y por los campos, y la gente salió a ver qué había pasado.
es.R: Los hombres que cuidaban los cerdos huyeron. Contaron a todos en el pueblo y en las granjas lo que había pasado. Entonces la gente salió para verlo con sus propios ojos.

sw.L: Na wale waliokuwa wakiwachunga walikimbia, wakatangaza habari mjini na mashambani; nao wakaja kuona ni nini kilichotokea.
sw.B: Wachungaji wa nguruwe walikimbia, wakaeneza habari mjini na mashambani, na watu wakaja kuona yaliyotokea.
sw.R: Wale watu waliokuwa wakichunga nguruwe walikimbia. Waliwaeleza watu wote wa mjini na wa mashambani yaliyotokea. Basi watu wakaja kujionea wenyewe.

decisions.choice: the city and the fields: the town and the farms around it
decisions.reason: The word for city is used for towns of any size. "Fields" means the farmland and villages around.

decisions.choice: they came: the people who heard
decisions.reason: The subject is the people of the town and the countryside.

decisions.choice: told everyone ... what had happened
decisions.reason: Readable says what they reported.

decisions.choice: la ciudad (L); el pueblo (B, R)
decisions.reason: The place was a town with its farms around it (meaning decision m1). Literal keeps "ciudad" for the Greek word; Balanced and Readable say "pueblo", since "ciudad" suggests a city, as in Matthew 8:33.

source.text: καὶ ἔρχονται πρὸς τὸν Ἰησοῦν, καὶ θεωροῦσιν τὸν δαιμονιζόμενον καθήμενον ἱματισμένον καὶ σωφρονοῦντα, τὸν ἐσχηκότα τὸν λεγιῶνα, καὶ ἐφοβήθησαν.

records.literal_gloss: And they come to the Jesus and see the one being demon-possessed sitting, clothed and being of sound mind, the one having had the legion, and they were afraid.

en.L: And they come to Jesus and see the demon-possessed man sitting, clothed and in his right mind, the one who had had the legion, and they were afraid.
en.B: When they reached Jesus, they found the man the demons had held sitting there with clothes on and in his right mind, the very man who had been held by the legion. And they were afraid.
en.R: They came to Jesus and saw the man who had had all those demons. He was sitting there with his clothes on, and his mind was clear again. This made the people afraid.

es.L: Y vienen a Jesús, y ven al endemoniado sentado, vestido y en su sano juicio, al que había tenido la legión, y tuvieron miedo.
es.B: Al llegar adonde estaba Jesús, encontraron sentado allí al hombre que habían dominado los demonios, vestido y en su sano juicio, el mismo que había estado en poder de la legión. Y tuvieron miedo.
es.R: Llegaron adonde estaba Jesús y vieron al hombre que antes tenía todos esos demonios. Estaba sentado, vestido, y su mente estaba clara otra vez. Eso hizo que la gente tuviera miedo.

sw.L: Nao wanakuja kwa Yesu, na wanamwona yule mwenye pepo ameketi, amevaa nguo, na ana akili timamu, yule aliyekuwa na legioni, nao wakaogopa.
sw.B: Walipofika kwa Yesu, walimkuta yule mtu aliyekuwa ametawaliwa na pepo ameketi pale, amevaa nguo, akiwa na akili zake timamu, yaani yule yule aliyekuwa ametawaliwa na legioni. Nao wakaogopa.
sw.R: Walifika kwa Yesu, wakamwona yule mtu aliyekuwa na pepo wale wote. Alikuwa ameketi pale, amevaa nguo, na akili zake zilikuwa zimerudi sawa. Jambo hilo liliwafanya watu waogope.

decisions.choice: the demon-possessed man: the one who had been possessed
decisions.reason: Mark keeps the description from before. The next words show that he is free now.

decisions.choice: clothed: he had gone without clothes before
decisions.reason: Mark does not say he was naked, but Luke 8:27 does. Being dressed is a sign of his return to normal life.

decisions.choice: of sound mind: sane, in control of himself
decisions.reason: The verb means to have a sound mind, the opposite of the raving he had shown (5:5).

decisions.choice: they were afraid: fear at a power beyond human control
decisions.reason: As the disciples feared after the storm (4:41), the people fear the one who has such power.

decisions.choice: they got to, they saw; they came, saw
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable use the past tense for the storytelling present.

decisions.choice: endemoniado (L); el hombre que habían dominado los demonios (B); el hombre que antes tenía todos esos demonios (R)
decisions.reason: The term used across the New Testament drafts is "demonio", as in Matthew 8:28. Literal keeps the one Greek word as one Spanish word; Balanced and Readable say plainly that he had been held by demons and is free now (meaning decision m1). The same in verses 16 and 18.

decisions.choice: mwenye pepo (L); aliyekuwa ametawaliwa na pepo (B); aliyekuwa na pepo (R)
decisions.reason: The term used across the New Testament drafts is "pepo" for a demon, as in Matthew 8:28. Balanced and Readable say in the past tense that the demons had held him (meaning decision m1), since he is free now. The same in verses 16 and 18.

source.text: καὶ διηγήσαντο αὐτοῖς οἱ ἰδόντες πῶς ἐγένετο τῷ δαιμονιζομένῳ καὶ περὶ τῶν χοίρων.

records.literal_gloss: And described to them those having seen how it happened to the one being demon-possessed, and concerning the pigs.

en.L: And those who had seen [it] described to them how it had happened to the demon-possessed man, and about the pigs.
en.B: Those who had seen it all told them what had happened to the man with the demons, and about the pigs too.
en.R: The people who had seen everything told the others what had happened to the man. They also told them about the pigs.

es.L: Y los que [lo] habían visto les contaron cómo le había sucedido al endemoniado, y lo de los cerdos.
es.B: Los que lo habían visto todo les contaron lo que le había pasado al hombre de los demonios, y también lo de los cerdos.
es.R: Los que habían visto todo les contaron a los demás lo que le había pasado al hombre. También les hablaron de los cerdos.

sw.L: Na wale walioona waliwaeleza jinsi ilivyompata yule mwenye pepo, na habari za nguruwe.
sw.B: Wale walioyaona yote waliwaeleza yaliyompata yule mtu mwenye pepo, na habari za nguruwe pia.
sw.R: Watu walioona kila kitu waliwaeleza wengine yaliyompata yule mtu. Waliwaeleza pia habari za nguruwe.

decisions.choice: those who had seen: the herdsmen and other witnesses
decisions.reason: Mark does not say who they were, only that they had seen it.

decisions.choice: and about the pigs: the loss of the herd is part of the report
decisions.reason: The people hear of both the man's cure and their loss, which leads to their request (5:17).

source.text: καὶ ἤρξαντο παρακαλεῖν αὐτὸν ἀπελθεῖν ἀπὸ τῶν ὁρίων αὐτῶν.

records.literal_gloss: And they began to beg him to depart from the region of them.

en.L: And they began to beg {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} to depart from their region.
en.B: Then they started pleading with Jesus to go away from their district.
en.R: Then the people begged Jesus to leave their land.

es.L: Y comenzaron a rogarle que se fuera de su territorio.
es.B: Entonces se pusieron a suplicar a Jesús que se marchara de su comarca.
es.R: Entonces la gente le rogó a Jesús que se fuera de su tierra.

sw.L: Nao wakaanza kumsihi aondoke mipakani mwao.
sw.B: Kisha wakaanza kumsihi Yesu aondoke katika eneo lao.
sw.R: Kisha watu walimsihi Yesu aondoke katika nchi yao.

decisions.choice: they began to beg: the people of the region
decisions.reason: Those who came out to see now ask Jesus to leave.

decisions.choice: to depart from their region: they would rather lose Jesus than face his power
alternatives: they were only angry about the pigs
decisions.reason: Mark gives no reason. Their fear (5:15) and their loss (5:16) are both in view.

source.text: καὶ ἐμβαίνοντος αὐτοῦ εἰς τὸ πλοῖον παρεκάλει αὐτὸν ὁ δαιμονισθεὶς ἵνα μετ’ αὐτοῦ ᾖ.

records.literal_gloss: And getting in of him into the boat, was begging him the one having been demon-possessed that with him he might be.

en.L: And as {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} was getting into the boat, the man who had been demon-possessed was begging {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} that he might be with {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.
en.B: As Jesus stepped into the boat, the man freed from the demons pleaded to go along with {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.
en.R: Jesus was stepping into the boat. Then the man who used to have the demons begged Jesus, "Please let me go with {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}!"

es.L: Y mientras {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} subía a la barca, el que había estado endemoniado {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} rogaba poder estar con {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}}.
es.B: Cuando Jesús subía a la barca, el hombre que había sido librado de los demonios {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} suplicaba que lo dejara ir con {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}}.
es.R: Jesús estaba subiendo a la barca. Entonces el hombre que antes tenía los demonios le rogó a Jesús: «¡Por favor, déjame ir contigo!».

sw.L: Na alipokuwa akipanda mashua, yule aliyekuwa amepagawa na pepo akamsihi ili awe pamoja {{deity_pronoun:naye|Naye}}.
sw.B: Yesu alipokuwa akipanda mashua, yule mtu aliyekuwa amewekwa huru kutoka kwa pepo alimsihi amruhusu aende pamoja {{deity_pronoun:naye|Naye}}.
sw.R: Yesu alikuwa akipanda mashua. Kisha yule mtu aliyekuwa na pepo zamani alimsihi Yesu, "Tafadhali niruhusu niende pamoja {{deity_pronoun:nawe|Nawe}}!"

decisions.choice: that he might be with him: to go with Jesus as a disciple
decisions.reason: "To be with him" is the phrase Mark used for the Twelve (3:14). The man asks to join those who follow Jesus.

decisions.choice: direct speech: Please let me go with you!
alternatives: that he might be with him
decisions.reason: Readable turns the request into direct speech.

source.text: καὶ οὐκ ἀφῆκεν αὐτόν, ἀλλὰ λέγει αὐτῷ· Ὕπαγε εἰς τὸν οἶκόν σου πρὸς τοὺς σούς, καὶ ἀπάγγειλον αὐτοῖς ὅσα ὁ κύριός σοι πεποίηκεν καὶ ἠλέησέν σε.

records.literal_gloss: And not he permitted him, but he says to him, Go to the home of you, to the your own, and report to them how much the Lord for you has done, and had mercy on you.

en.L: And {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} did not permit him, but {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} says to him, "Go to your home, to your own [people], and report to them how much the Lord has done for you, and [how] {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} had mercy on you."
en.B: But Jesus would not let him, and told him instead, "Go home to your own people, and let them know all that the Lord has done for you, and the mercy {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} has shown you."
en.R: But Jesus did not let him come. Jesus told him, "Go home to your family. Tell them all that the Lord has done for you. Tell them how kind {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} has been to you."

es.L: Y no se lo permitió, sino que le dice: «Ve a tu casa, a los tuyos, y anúnciales cuánto ha hecho el Señor por ti, y [cómo] tuvo misericordia de ti».
es.B: Pero Jesús no se lo permitió, sino que le dijo: «Vete a casa, con tu gente, y cuéntales todo lo que el Señor ha hecho por ti y cómo ha tenido compasión de ti».
es.R: Pero Jesús no se lo permitió. Le dijo: «Vete a tu casa, con tu familia. Cuéntales todo lo que el Señor ha hecho por ti. Cuéntales lo bueno que ha sido contigo».

sw.L: Naye hakumruhusu, bali anamwambia, "Nenda nyumbani kwako, kwa watu wako, ukawaarifu yote ambayo Bwana amekutendea, na [jinsi] alivyokuhurumia."
sw.B: Lakini Yesu hakumruhusu, bali alimwambia, "Nenda nyumbani kwa watu wako, ukawajulishe yote ambayo Bwana amekutendea, na jinsi alivyokuonea huruma."
sw.R: Lakini Yesu hakumruhusu. Alimwambia, "Nenda nyumbani kwa jamaa zako. Waambie yote ambayo Bwana amekutendea. Waambie jinsi alivyokuwa mwema kwako."

decisions.choice: the Lord: God
decisions.reason: Jesus points to God as the one who has acted. In 5:20 the man tells what Jesus did: in Jesus, God has acted.

decisions.choice: go and report: here Jesus sends the man to tell
alternatives: Jesus breaks his own rule of silence
decisions.reason: Elsewhere Jesus forbids people to tell (1:44; 5:43). In Gentile country, away from the crowds of Galilee, he sends this man home to tell what God has done.

decisions.choice: your own: your family and people
decisions.reason: The phrase means those who belong to him: his household and relatives.

decisions.choice: had mercy: showed pity and acted to help
decisions.reason: The verb is used for the pity that moves someone to help (10:47-48).

decisions.choice: how kind he has been to you
decisions.reason: Readable uses a plainer phrase for mercy.

decisions.choice: no deity_pronoun span on alivyokuhurumia, alivyokuonea huruma, alivyokuwa mwema (how he had mercy)
decisions.reason: The English "he", the Lord, takes the setting. Swahili carries it in the subject prefix a- of the verb, which cannot take a capital, so there is nothing for the setting to change.

source.text: καὶ ἀπῆλθεν καὶ ἤρξατο κηρύσσειν ἐν τῇ Δεκαπόλει ὅσα ἐποίησεν αὐτῷ ὁ Ἰησοῦς, καὶ πάντες ἐθαύμαζον.

records.literal_gloss: And he departed and began to proclaim in the Decapolis how much did for him the Jesus, and all were marveling.

en.L: And he went away and began to proclaim in the Decapolis how much Jesus had done for him, and everyone was amazed.
en.B: So he went off and started to tell all through the Decapolis the great things Jesus had done for him. Everyone who heard was astonished.
en.R: So the man left. He went through the area called the Ten Towns, the Decapolis, and told people how much Jesus had done for him. Everyone was amazed.

es.L: Y se fue y comenzó a proclamar en la Decápolis cuánto había hecho Jesús por él, y todos se maravillaban.
es.B: Así que se fue y comenzó a contar por toda la Decápolis las grandes cosas que Jesús había hecho por él. Todos los que lo oían quedaban asombrados.
es.R: Entonces el hombre se fue. Recorrió la región llamada las Diez Ciudades, la Decápolis, y le contaba a la gente todo lo que Jesús había hecho por él. Todos se quedaban asombrados.

sw.L: Naye akaenda zake, akaanza kutangaza katika Dekapoli yote ambayo Yesu alimtendea, na watu wote walikuwa wakistaajabu.
sw.B: Basi aliondoka, akaanza kueneza habari katika Dekapoli yote juu ya mambo makuu ambayo Yesu alikuwa amemtendea. Kila aliyesikia alishangaa.
sw.R: Basi yule mtu aliondoka. Alikwenda katika eneo lililoitwa Miji Kumi, yaani Dekapoli, akawaeleza watu yote ambayo Yesu alimtendea. Watu wote walishangaa.

decisions.choice: the Decapolis: a league of ten Greek cities, mostly east of the Jordan
decisions.reason: The name means Ten Cities. They were Gentile cities of Greek culture, including Gerasa and Gadara.

decisions.choice: proclaim: announce publicly
decisions.reason: Mark uses the same verb for John, Jesus and the disciples (1:4, 14; 3:14). The healed man becomes a herald.

decisions.choice: how much Jesus had done: told to report what the Lord did (5:19), he tells what Jesus did
decisions.reason: Mark sets "the Lord" in 5:19 beside "Jesus" here without comment. The reader is left to see that God's work is done through Jesus.

decisions.choice: the area called the Ten Towns, the Decapolis
decisions.reason: Readable explains the name.

source.text: Καὶ διαπεράσαντος τοῦ Ἰησοῦ ἐν τῷ πλοίῳ πάλιν εἰς τὸ πέραν συνήχθη ὄχλος πολὺς ἐπ’ αὐτόν, καὶ ἦν παρὰ τὴν θάλασσαν.

records.literal_gloss: And having crossed over the Jesus in the boat again to the other side, was gathered a crowd great to him, and he was beside the sea.

en.L: And when Jesus had crossed over again in the boat to the other side, a great crowd gathered around {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} was beside the sea.
en.B: When Jesus had gone back across by boat, a large crowd gathered around {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} while {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} was still by the lake.
en.R: Jesus went back across Lake Galilee in the boat. A big crowd came together around {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} as {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} stood on the shore.

es.L: Y habiendo cruzado Jesús de nuevo en la barca al otro lado, se reunió junto a {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} una gran multitud, y estaba junto al mar.
es.B: Cuando Jesús volvió a cruzar en la barca a la otra orilla, una gran multitud se reunió a {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} alrededor mientras {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} estaba todavía junto al lago.
es.R: Jesús volvió a cruzar el lago de Galilea en la barca. Una gran multitud se juntó a {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} alrededor mientras estaba en la orilla.

sw.L: Na Yesu alipokwisha kuvuka tena kwa mashua kwenda ng'ambo, umati mkubwa ulikusanyika {{deity_pronoun:kwake|Kwake}}, naye alikuwa kando ya bahari.
sw.B: Yesu alipokwisha kuvuka tena kwa mashua kwenda ng'ambo, umati mkubwa wa watu ulikusanyika kumzunguka, alipokuwa bado kando ya ziwa.
sw.R: Yesu alivuka Ziwa Galilaya tena kwa mashua. Umati mkubwa wa watu ulikusanyika {{deity_pronoun:kwake|Kwake}} alipokuwa amesimama ufuoni.

decisions.choice: to the other side: back to the western, Jewish shore
decisions.reason: Jesus returns to Galilee, where the crowds wait for him (4:1).

decisions.choice: in the boat, as the SBLGNT reads
decisions.reason: A few early manuscripts lack "in the boat". The sense is the same either way. Reviewers should check this against the SBLGNT apparatus.

decisions.choice: on the shore
decisions.reason: Readable calls the lakeside the shore.

source.text: καὶ ἔρχεται εἷς τῶν ἀρχισυναγώγων, ὀνόματι Ἰάϊρος, καὶ ἰδὼν αὐτὸν πίπτει πρὸς τοὺς πόδας αὐτοῦ καὶ παρακαλεῖ αὐτὸν πολλὰ λέγων ὅτι Τὸ θυγάτριόν μου ἐσχάτως ἔχει, ἵνα ἐλθὼν ἐπιθῇς τὰς χεῖρας αὐτῇ ἵνα σωθῇ καὶ ζήσῃ.

records.literal_gloss: And comes one of the synagogue leaders, by name Jairus, and having seen him falls at the feet of him \v 23 and begs him much saying that, The little daughter of me at the end is holding, that having come you would lay the hands on her so that she may be saved and live.

en.L: And one of the synagogue leaders, Jairus by name, comes, and seeing {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} he falls at {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} feet \v 23 and begs {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} earnestly, saying, "My little daughter is at the point of death. [I beg {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}] that {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} come and lay [{{deity_pronoun:your|Your}}] hands on her, so that she may be saved and live."
en.B: One of the leaders of the synagogue, a man named Jairus, came up. When he saw Jesus, he threw himself at {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} feet \v 23 and pleaded with {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} again and again. "My little daughter is dying," he said. "Please come and put {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} hands on her, so that she may get well and live."
en.R: A man named Jairus came. He was one of the leaders of the local synagogue. When Jairus saw Jesus, he bowed down at {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} feet. \v 23 He begged Jesus over and over, "My little girl is about to die. Please come and put {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} hands on her. Then she will get well and live!"

es.L: Y viene uno de los jefes de la sinagoga, llamado Jairo, y al verlo cae a {{deity_pronoun:sus|Sus}} pies \v 23 y {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} ruega mucho, diciendo: «Mi hijita está en las últimas. [Te ruego] que vengas y pongas las manos sobre ella, para que sea salvada y viva».
es.B: Llegó entonces uno de los jefes de la sinagoga, un hombre llamado Jairo. Al ver a Jesús, se echó a {{deity_pronoun:sus|Sus}} pies \v 23 y {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} suplicó con insistencia: «Mi hijita se está muriendo. Por favor, ven y pon {{deity_pronoun:tus|Tus}} manos sobre ella para que se sane y viva».
es.R: Llegó un hombre llamado Jairo. Era uno de los jefes de la sinagoga del lugar. Cuando Jairo vio a Jesús, se arrodilló a {{deity_pronoun:sus|Sus}} pies. \v 23 Le rogaba a Jesús una y otra vez: «Mi niña está a punto de morir. Por favor, ven y pon {{deity_pronoun:tus|Tus}} manos sobre ella. ¡Así se curará y vivirá!».

sw.L: Na anakuja mmoja wa wakuu wa sinagogi, jina lake Yairo, na alipomwona anaanguka miguuni {{deity_pronoun:pake|Pake}} \v 23 na anamsihi sana, akisema, "Binti yangu mdogo yu katika hali ya kufa. [Nakusihi] uje uweke mikono [{{deity_pronoun:yako|Yako}}] juu yake, ili aokoke na kuishi."
sw.B: Kisha akaja mmoja wa viongozi wa sinagogi, mtu aitwaye Yairo. Alipomwona Yesu, alijitupa miguuni {{deity_pronoun:pake|Pake}} \v 23 akamsihi tena na tena, "Binti yangu mdogo anakufa. Tafadhali njoo umwekee mikono {{deity_pronoun:yako|Yako}}, ili apone na kuishi."
sw.R: Mtu mmoja aitwaye Yairo alikuja. Alikuwa mmoja wa viongozi wa sinagogi la mahali pale. Yairo alipomwona Yesu, alipiga magoti miguuni {{deity_pronoun:pake|Pake}}. \v 23 Alimsihi Yesu tena na tena, "Binti yangu mdogo yu karibu kufa. Tafadhali njoo umwekee mikono {{deity_pronoun:yako|Yako}}. Hapo atapona na kuishi!"

decisions.choice: synagogue leader: the man in charge of the synagogue's meetings
decisions.reason: A synagogue leader arranged worship and chose who would read and teach. He was a respected man in the town.

decisions.choice: is holding at the end: is at the point of death
decisions.reason: The phrase means near the end of life. She is still alive (5:35).

decisions.choice: be saved: be made well, rescued from death
decisions.reason: The verb is used both for healing and for God's saving. Here it means rescued from her illness, set beside "live"; the wider sense may be heard too.

decisions.choice: that you would come and lay: an urgent request without a main verb
decisions.reason: The clause stands on its own as a plea. "I beg you" is understood.

decisions.choice: lay hands on her: touch to heal and bless
decisions.reason: Laying on of hands was a sign of blessing and was expected from a healer (6:5; 8:23).

decisions.choice: get well
decisions.reason: In a request for a sick child, Balanced and Readable use the healing sense. Literal keeps the word that can also mean salvation.

decisions.choice: one of the leaders of the local synagogue
decisions.reason: Readable makes clear that he led a local meeting place.

decisions.choice: sea salvada (L); se sane (B); se curará (R)
decisions.reason: As in Matthew 9:21: Literal keeps the verb "salvar", which says more than getting well (meaning decision m3); Balanced and Readable say what Jairus asks for. The same in verses 28 and 34.

decisions.choice: uno de los jefes de la sinagoga
decisions.reason: The man in charge of the synagogue's meetings (meaning decision m1). "Jefe de la sinagoga" says plainly that he led it, and matches "los jefes de los sacerdotes" on the term sheet. The same in verses 35, 36 and 38.

decisions.choice: aokoke (L); apone (B, R)
decisions.reason: The verb means to be made well and more than that, rescued (meaning decision m3). "Kuokoka" means both to recover and to be saved, so Literal keeps the double sense, as in Matthew 9:21; Balanced and Readable say what Jairus asks for. The same in verses 28 and 34.

decisions.choice: mkuu wa sinagogi (L); kiongozi wa sinagogi (B, R)
decisions.reason: The man in charge of the synagogue's meetings (meaning decision m1). Literal keeps "mkuu" (head) for the Greek title; Balanced and Readable say "kiongozi" (leader), the everyday word, as the English does. The same in verses 35, 36 and 38.

source.text: καὶ ἀπῆλθεν μετ’ αὐτοῦ.

records.literal_gloss: And he went with him.

en.L: And {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} went with him.
en.B: So Jesus set out with him.
en.R: So Jesus went with Jairus.

es.L: Y se fue con él.
es.B: Así que Jesús se puso en camino con él.
es.R: Entonces Jesús fue con Jairo.

sw.L: Naye akaenda pamoja naye.
sw.B: Basi Yesu akaondoka pamoja naye.
sw.R: Basi Yesu alikwenda pamoja na Yairo.

decisions.choice: him: Jairus
decisions.reason: Jesus goes with the father to his house.

source.text: Καὶ ἠκολούθει αὐτῷ ὄχλος πολύς, καὶ συνέθλιβον αὐτόν.

records.literal_gloss: And was following him a crowd great, and were pressing around him.

en.L: And a great crowd was following {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, and they were pressing around {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.
en.B: A huge crowd went along behind {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, jostling {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} on every side.
en.R: A big crowd followed {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}. People were pushing against {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} from all sides.

es.L: Y {{deity_pronoun:lo|Lo}} seguía una gran multitud, y {{deity_pronoun:lo|Lo}} apretujaban.
es.B: Una enorme multitud {{deity_pronoun:lo|Lo}} seguía y {{deity_pronoun:lo|Lo}} apretujaba por todos lados.
es.R: Una gran multitud {{deity_pronoun:lo|Lo}} seguía. La gente se apretaba contra {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} por todos lados.

sw.L: Na umati mkubwa ulikuwa ukimfuata, na walikuwa wakimsonga.
sw.B: Umati mkubwa wa watu ulimfuata, ukimsongasonga kila upande.
sw.R: Umati mkubwa ulimfuata. Watu walikuwa wakimsukuma kutoka pande zote.

decisions.choice: pressing around: crushing in on him
decisions.reason: The verb means to press hard from all sides. It explains the disciples' answer in 5:31.

source.text: καὶ γυνὴ οὖσα ἐν ῥύσει αἵματος δώδεκα ἔτη καὶ πολλὰ παθοῦσα ὑπὸ πολλῶν ἰατρῶν καὶ δαπανήσασα τὰ παρ’ αὐτῆς πάντα καὶ μηδὲν ὠφεληθεῖσα ἀλλὰ μᾶλλον εἰς τὸ χεῖρον ἐλθοῦσα, ἀκούσασα περὶ τοῦ Ἰησοῦ, ἐλθοῦσα ἐν τῷ ὄχλῳ ὄπισθεν ἥψατο τοῦ ἱματίου αὐτοῦ·

records.literal_gloss: And a woman being with a flow of blood twelve years \v 26 and many [things] having suffered under many physicians and having spent the from her all and nothing having benefited but rather to the worse having come, \v 27 having heard concerning the Jesus, having come in the crowd behind, touched the garment of him.

en.L: And a woman who had had a flow of blood [for] twelve years, \v 26 and had suffered much under many physicians, and had spent all that she had, and had not benefited at all but rather had grown worse, \v 27 having heard about Jesus, came up in the crowd behind [{{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}] and touched {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} garment.
en.B: In the crowd was a woman who had been bleeding for twelve years. \v 26 She had gone through a great deal at the hands of many doctors and had spent everything she owned. Instead of getting better, she had only grown worse. \v 27 She had heard about Jesus, so she made her way through the crowd and touched {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} cloak from behind.
en.R: A woman was there who had been sick with bleeding for twelve years. \v 26 Many doctors had tried to help her, and they had caused her a lot of pain. She had spent all her money on them. But she was not getting better. She was getting worse. \v 27 This woman had heard about Jesus. So she pushed through the crowd and touched {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} coat from behind.

es.L: Y una mujer que estaba con flujo de sangre [desde hacía] doce años, \v 26 y había sufrido mucho a manos de muchos médicos, y había gastado todo lo que tenía, y en nada se había beneficiado, sino que más bien había ido a peor, \v 27 habiendo oído acerca de Jesús, vino entre la multitud por detrás [de {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}}] y tocó {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} manto.
es.B: Entre la multitud había una mujer que llevaba doce años con hemorragias. \v 26 Había sufrido mucho en manos de muchos médicos y había gastado todo lo que tenía. En lugar de mejorar, solo había empeorado. \v 27 Como había oído hablar de Jesús, se abrió paso entre la gente y tocó {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} manto por detrás.
es.R: Había allí una mujer que llevaba doce años enferma: sangraba sin parar. \v 26 Muchos médicos habían tratado de ayudarla, y le habían causado mucho dolor. Había gastado todo su dinero en ellos. Pero no mejoraba. Iba cada vez peor. \v 27 Esta mujer había oído hablar de Jesús. Así que se abrió paso entre la multitud y tocó {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} ropa por detrás.

sw.L: Na mwanamke mmoja aliyekuwa na ugonjwa wa kutokwa damu kwa miaka kumi na miwili, \v 26 na aliyekuwa ameteseka sana chini ya matabibu wengi, na kutumia vyote alivyokuwa navyo, wala hakufaidika kitu, bali hali yake ilizidi kuwa mbaya, \v 27 aliposikia habari za Yesu, alikuja katika umati kwa nyuma [{{deity_pronoun:yake|Yake}}], akaligusa vazi {{deity_pronoun:lake|Lake}}.
sw.B: Katika umati huo alikuwemo mwanamke aliyekuwa akitokwa damu kwa miaka kumi na miwili. \v 26 Alikuwa ameteseka sana mikononi mwa matabibu wengi, na alikuwa ametumia mali yake yote. Badala ya kupata nafuu, hali yake ilizidi kuwa mbaya. \v 27 Alikuwa amesikia habari za Yesu, kwa hiyo alipenya katikati ya umati, akaligusa joho {{deity_pronoun:lake|Lake}} kwa nyuma.
sw.R: Kulikuwa na mwanamke mmoja pale aliyekuwa mgonjwa kwa miaka kumi na miwili; alikuwa akitokwa damu. \v 26 Madaktari wengi walijaribu kumsaidia, lakini walimsababishia maumivu mengi. Alikuwa ametumia fedha zake zote kwao. Lakini hakupata nafuu. Hali yake ilizidi kuwa mbaya. \v 27 Mwanamke huyo alikuwa amesikia habari za Yesu. Kwa hiyo alipenya katikati ya umati, akagusa nguo {{deity_pronoun:zake|Zake}} kwa nyuma.

decisions.choice: a flow of blood: continual bleeding, most likely from the womb
decisions.reason: The phrase is the one used in Leviticus 15:25 for a woman's bleeding outside her monthly period.

decisions.choice: a flow of blood: in the law of Moses it made her unclean
decisions.reason: Under Leviticus 15:25-27 she was unclean all those years, and so was anything she touched. That is why she came from behind in secret.

decisions.choice: one long sentence of participles leading to she touched
decisions.reason: Mark piles up seven participles describing her story before the one main verb, touched.

decisions.choice: suffered much under many physicians: the treatments themselves hurt her
decisions.reason: Medicine of the time could be painful. Mark notes that it cost her everything and did no good.

decisions.choice: garment: the outer cloak
decisions.reason: The word is used for the outer robe. Matthew 9:20 and Luke 8:44 say she touched its fringe.

decisions.choice: the sentence is broken into several
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable break the chain of participles into separate sentences.

decisions.choice: Many doctors had tried to help her, and they had caused her a lot of pain
alternatives: had suffered much under many physicians
decisions.reason: Readable spells out what suffering under doctors meant.

decisions.choice: matabibu (L, B); madaktari (R)
decisions.reason: "Waganga" today often means traditional healers, which would add a picture the Greek does not have. "Tabibu" is the standard word for a physician; Readable uses the everyday "daktari".

decisions.choice: vazi (L); joho (B); nguo (R)
decisions.reason: The outer cloak (meaning decision m5), worded as in Matthew 9:20-21: "joho" is the long outer robe, and Readable says simply "clothes". The same in verses 28 and 30.

source.text: ἔλεγεν γὰρ ὅτι Ἐὰν ἅψωμαι κἂν τῶν ἱματίων αὐτοῦ σωθήσομαι.

records.literal_gloss: She was saying for that, If I touch even the garments of him, I will be saved.

en.L: For she was saying, "If I touch even {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} garments, I will be saved."
en.B: She kept telling herself, "Even if all I touch is {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} clothes, I will be made well."
en.R: She thought, "If I can only touch {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} clothes, I will get well."

es.L: Porque decía: «Si toco aunque sea {{deity_pronoun:sus|Sus}} vestidos, seré salvada».
es.B: Se decía a sí misma: «Aunque solo toque {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} ropa, quedaré sana».
es.R: Pensaba: «Si consigo tocar aunque sea {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} ropa, me curaré».

sw.L: Kwa maana alikuwa akisema, "Nikigusa hata mavazi {{deity_pronoun:yake|Yake}}, nitaokoka."
sw.B: Alikuwa akijiambia, "Hata nikigusa mavazi {{deity_pronoun:yake|Yake}} tu, nitapona."
sw.R: Alifikiri, "Nikiweza kugusa nguo {{deity_pronoun:zake|Zake}} tu, nitapona."

decisions.choice: she was saying: saying to herself
decisions.reason: The verb is continuous: she kept saying this, most likely to herself.

decisions.choice: I will be saved: I will be made well
decisions.reason: As in 5:23, the verb means rescue from her illness; Jesus' reply in 5:34 uses the same verb and lets its wider sense be heard.

decisions.choice: even: even his clothes, if not himself
decisions.reason: The word means "even" or "if only". She dares not ask him directly.

decisions.choice: be made well (B); get well (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable use the healing sense, which is what she has in mind.

source.text: καὶ εὐθὺς ἐξηράνθη ἡ πηγὴ τοῦ αἵματος αὐτῆς, καὶ ἔγνω τῷ σώματι ὅτι ἴαται ἀπὸ τῆς μάστιγος.

records.literal_gloss: And immediately was dried up the source of the blood of her, and she knew in the body that she has been healed from the affliction.

en.L: And immediately the source of her blood was dried up, and she knew in [her] body that she had been healed of the affliction.
en.B: At once her bleeding stopped, and she could feel in her body that she was free of her suffering.
en.R: Right away her bleeding stopped. She could feel in her body that she was healed.

es.L: Y en seguida se secó la fuente de su sangre, y sintió en el cuerpo que había sido sanada de la aflicción.
es.B: Al instante se le detuvo la hemorragia, y sintió en su cuerpo que estaba libre de su sufrimiento.
es.R: En seguida dejó de sangrar. Sintió en su cuerpo que estaba sana.

sw.L: Na mara chemchemi ya damu yake ikakauka, naye akatambua mwilini mwake kwamba ameponywa ugonjwa ule.
sw.B: Mara damu yake ikaacha kutoka, naye akahisi mwilini mwake kwamba amepona mateso yake.
sw.R: Mara moja damu ikaacha kutoka. Aliweza kuhisi mwilini mwake kwamba amepona.

decisions.choice: source: the place the bleeding came from
decisions.reason: The word means a spring or fountain. Leviticus 12:7 uses it for a woman's bleeding.

decisions.choice: affliction: a disease, literally a whip or scourge
decisions.reason: The word means a whip, and was used for a painful illness (3:10). It does not say the illness was a punishment.

decisions.choice: she knew: she could feel it
decisions.reason: She is certain from what she feels in her body.

source.text: καὶ εὐθὺς ὁ Ἰησοῦς ἐπιγνοὺς ἐν ἑαυτῷ τὴν ἐξ αὐτοῦ δύναμιν ἐξελθοῦσαν ἐπιστραφεὶς ἐν τῷ ὄχλῳ ἔλεγεν· Τίς μου ἥψατο τῶν ἱματίων;

records.literal_gloss: And immediately the Jesus having known in himself the out of him power having gone out, having turned around in the crowd he was saying, Who of me touched the garments?

en.L: And immediately Jesus, knowing in {{deity_pronoun:himself|Himself}} that power had gone out from {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, turned around in the crowd and was saying, "Who touched {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} garments?"
en.B: Right away Jesus knew within {{deity_pronoun:himself|Himself}} that power had gone out of {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}. He turned around in the crowd and said, "Who touched {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} clothes?"
en.R: At that moment Jesus knew that power had gone out from {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}. So {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} turned to face the people and asked, "Who touched {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} clothes?"

es.L: Y en seguida Jesús, conociendo en {{deity_pronoun:sí mismo|Sí mismo}} el poder que había salido de {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}}, volviéndose entre la multitud, decía: «¿Quién tocó {{deity_pronoun:mis|Mis}} vestidos?».
es.B: Al instante Jesús sintió dentro de {{deity_pronoun:sí mismo|Sí mismo}} que de {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} había salido poder. Se volvió hacia la multitud y preguntó: «¿Quién tocó {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} ropa?».
es.R: En ese momento Jesús supo que había salido poder de {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}}. Así que se volvió hacia la gente y preguntó: «¿Quién tocó {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} ropa?».

sw.L: Na mara Yesu, akitambua nafsini {{deity_pronoun:mwake|Mwake}} kwamba nguvu imemtoka, akageuka katikati ya umati, akawa akisema, "Nani aliyegusa mavazi {{deity_pronoun:yangu|Yangu}}?"
sw.B: Mara Yesu alitambua nafsini {{deity_pronoun:mwake|Mwake}} kwamba nguvu imemtoka. Aligeuka katikati ya umati, akasema, "Ni nani aliyegusa mavazi {{deity_pronoun:yangu|Yangu}}?"
sw.R: Wakati huo huo Yesu alijua kwamba nguvu imemtoka. Basi akageuka kuwatazama watu, akauliza, "Ni nani aliyegusa nguo {{deity_pronoun:zangu|Zangu}}?"

decisions.choice: power: the power to heal
decisions.reason: The word is the one Mark uses for miracles (6:2, 5). Healing power went out from Jesus.

decisions.choice: knowing in himself: he was aware of it within
decisions.reason: Jesus knew at once, without being told.

decisions.choice: who touched my garments: Jesus asks in order to meet her
alternatives: Jesus did not know who it was
decisions.reason: Mark does not explain whether Jesus knew. His question brings the woman forward to be seen and spoken to (5:33-34).

source.text: καὶ ἔλεγον αὐτῷ οἱ μαθηταὶ αὐτοῦ· Βλέπεις τὸν ὄχλον συνθλίβοντά σε, καὶ λέγεις· Τίς μου ἥψατο;

records.literal_gloss: And were saying to him the disciples of him, You see the crowd pressing around you, and you say, Who of me touched?

en.L: And {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} disciples were saying to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, "You see the crowd pressing around {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}, and {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} say, 'Who touched {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}?'"
en.B: His disciples said to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, "You can see how the crowd is crushing in on {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}. How can {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} ask, 'Who touched {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}?'"
en.R: His followers said, "Look at all these people pushing against {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}! How can {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} ask, 'Who touched {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}?'"

es.L: Y {{deity_pronoun:sus|Sus}} discípulos {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} decían: «Ves a la multitud que {{deity_pronoun:te|Te}} apretuja, y dices: “¿Quién {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} tocó?”».
es.B: Sus discípulos {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} dijeron: «Ya ves cómo la multitud {{deity_pronoun:te|Te}} apretuja. ¿Cómo puedes preguntar: “¿Quién {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} tocó?”?».
es.R: Sus discípulos le dijeron: «¡Mira cuánta gente {{deity_pronoun:te|Te}} está empujando! ¿Cómo puedes preguntar: “¿Quién {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} tocó?”?».

sw.L: Na wanafunzi {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}} walikuwa wakimwambia, "Unauona umati unavyokusonga, {{deity_pronoun:nawe|Nawe}} unasema, 'Nani aliyenigusa?'"
sw.B: Wanafunzi {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}} wakamwambia, "Unaona jinsi umati unavyokusonga. Unawezaje kuuliza, 'Ni nani aliyenigusa?'"
sw.R: Wanafunzi {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}} wakamwambia, "Tazama watu wote hawa wanaokusukuma! Unawezaje kuuliza, 'Ni nani aliyenigusa?'"

decisions.choice: you see ... and you say: a reproachful question
decisions.reason: The disciples think the question makes no sense with so many people touching him.

decisions.choice: How can you ask
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable make the disciples' surprise plain.

source.text: καὶ περιεβλέπετο ἰδεῖν τὴν τοῦτο ποιήσασαν.

records.literal_gloss: And he was looking around to see the one this having done.

en.L: And {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} was looking around to see the [woman] who had done this.
en.B: But Jesus went on searching the faces around {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} for the one who had done it.
en.R: But Jesus kept looking at the people around {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} to find out who had touched {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.

es.L: Y miraba alrededor para ver a la que había hecho esto.
es.B: Pero Jesús seguía mirando a {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} alrededor, buscando a la que lo había hecho.
es.R: Pero Jesús siguió mirando a la gente que estaba a {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} alrededor, para saber quién {{deity_pronoun:lo|Lo}} había tocado.

sw.L: Naye alikuwa akitazama pande zote ili amwone yule [mwanamke] aliyefanya jambo hili.
sw.B: Lakini Yesu aliendelea kutazama huku na huku ili amwone yule aliyefanya hivyo.
sw.R: Lakini Yesu aliendelea kuwatazama watu waliomzunguka ili ajue ni nani aliyemgusa.

decisions.choice: the one who had done this: the participle is feminine
alternatives: Jesus knew she was a woman
decisions.reason: The Greek form is feminine. Mark the narrator knows it was a woman; it does not say whether Jesus did.

decisions.choice: was looking around: he kept looking
decisions.reason: The verb is continuous: he did not give up searching.

decisions.choice: [woman]
decisions.reason: Literal shows the feminine form with a bracketed word.

decisions.choice: a la que, with no word for "woman"
decisions.reason: The Greek participle is feminine (meaning decision m1). The English Literal needs to supply [woman]; the Spanish feminine article "la" already shows it, so nothing is supplied.

source.text: ἡ δὲ γυνὴ φοβηθεῖσα καὶ τρέμουσα, εἰδυῖα ὃ γέγονεν αὐτῇ, ἦλθεν καὶ προσέπεσεν αὐτῷ καὶ εἶπεν αὐτῷ πᾶσαν τὴν ἀλήθειαν.

records.literal_gloss: The and woman, having been afraid and trembling, knowing what had happened to her, came and fell down before him and told him all the truth.

en.L: And the woman, frightened and trembling, knowing what had happened to her, came and fell down before {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} and told {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} the whole truth.
en.B: Then the woman, afraid and shaking, knowing what had been done for her, came forward, dropped down before {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, and told {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} the whole truth.
en.R: The woman knew what had happened to her. She was afraid and shaking. She came and bowed down in front of Jesus. Then she told {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} the whole truth.

es.L: Y la mujer, asustada y temblando, sabiendo lo que le había sucedido, vino y se postró ante {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} y {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} dijo toda la verdad.
es.B: Entonces la mujer, con miedo y temblando, sabiendo lo que había ocurrido en ella, se acercó, cayó de rodillas ante {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} y {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} contó toda la verdad.
es.R: La mujer sabía lo que le había pasado. Tenía miedo y temblaba. Se acercó y se arrodilló delante de Jesús. Entonces {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} contó toda la verdad.

sw.L: Lakini yule mwanamke, akiwa na hofu na kutetemeka, akijua lililompata, alikuja, akaanguka mbele {{deity_pronoun:yake|Yake}}, akamweleza kweli yote.
sw.B: Kisha yule mwanamke, akiogopa na kutetemeka, akijua aliyotendewa, alikuja, akapiga magoti mbele {{deity_pronoun:yake|Yake}}, akamweleza ukweli wote.
sw.R: Yule mwanamke alijua yaliyompata. Aliogopa, akatetemeka. Alikuja, akainama mbele ya Yesu. Kisha akamweleza ukweli wote.

decisions.choice: frightened and trembling: awe as well as fear
decisions.reason: She may have feared blame for touching him while unclean. The same words are used for awe before God's power.

decisions.choice: the whole truth: everything that had happened
decisions.reason: She tells her whole story openly, before the crowd.

source.text: ὁ δὲ εἶπεν αὐτῇ· Θυγάτηρ, ἡ πίστις σου σέσωκέν σε· ὕπαγε εἰς εἰρήνην, καὶ ἴσθι ὑγιὴς ἀπὸ τῆς μάστιγός σου.

records.literal_gloss: He and said to her, Daughter, the faith of you has saved you; go in peace, and be healthy from the affliction of you.

en.L: And {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} said to her, "Daughter, your faith has saved you. Go in peace, and be healthy, [free] from your affliction."
en.B: "Daughter," {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} told her, "your faith has saved you and made you well. Go in peace, free of your suffering."
en.R: Jesus said to her, "My daughter, your faith has made you well and saved you. Go in peace. Your sickness is gone for good."

es.L: Y {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} le dijo: «Hija, tu fe te ha salvado; ve en paz, y queda sana, [libre] de tu aflicción».
es.B: «Hija —le dijo {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}}—, tu fe te ha salvado y te ha sanado. Vete en paz, libre de tu sufrimiento».
es.R: Jesús le dijo: «Hija mía, tu fe te ha sanado y te ha salvado. Vete en paz. Tu enfermedad se ha ido para siempre».

sw.L: Naye akamwambia, "Binti, imani yako imekuokoa; nenda kwa amani, na uwe mzima, [huru] kutoka katika ugonjwa wako."
sw.B: Akamwambia, "Binti, imani yako imekuokoa na kukuponya. Nenda kwa amani, ukiwa huru kutoka katika mateso yako."
sw.R: Yesu akamwambia, "Binti yangu, imani yako imekuponya na kukuokoa. Nenda kwa amani. Ugonjwa wako umekwisha kabisa."

decisions.choice: has saved: has made well, and more
decisions.reason: The verb is the one she used in 5:28, which means both healing and rescue by God. Her body is healed already (5:29); Jesus' words also give her a place restored before God and the people.

decisions.choice: faith: trust in Jesus to heal
decisions.reason: Her faith is shown in what she did: reaching out to Jesus. Jesus credits her faith, not her touch or the cloak.

decisions.choice: go in peace: a farewell and blessing
decisions.reason: The words are a common Jewish farewell (1 Samuel 1:17). Peace means wholeness and well-being.

decisions.choice: daughter: a word of warmth and of welcome
decisions.reason: Jesus calls the unclean woman "daughter", taking her into the family of God's people (3:35).

decisions.choice: be healthy from your affliction: stay healed
decisions.reason: Jesus confirms that the cure is real and lasting.

decisions.choice: saved you and made you well (B); made you well and saved you (R)
decisions.reason: One English verb cannot carry both senses, so Balanced and Readable use two. Literal keeps the single verb.

source.text: Ἔτι αὐτοῦ λαλοῦντος ἔρχονται ἀπὸ τοῦ ἀρχισυναγώγου λέγοντες ὅτι Ἡ θυγάτηρ σου ἀπέθανεν· τί ἔτι σκύλλεις τὸν διδάσκαλον;

records.literal_gloss: Still him speaking, they come from the synagogue leader saying that, The daughter of you died; why still trouble the teacher?

en.L: While {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} was still speaking, they come from the [house of the] synagogue leader, saying, "Your daughter has died. Why trouble the teacher any longer?"
en.B: While Jesus was still talking, some people arrived from the synagogue leader's house. "Your daughter is dead," they said. "There is no need to bother the teacher any more."
en.R: Jesus was still speaking when some people came from Jairus's house. They said to Jairus, "Your daughter has died. Do not make the teacher come now."

es.L: Mientras {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} aún hablaba, llegan de [la casa] del jefe de la sinagoga, diciendo: «Tu hija ha muerto; ¿para qué molestas todavía al Maestro?».
es.B: Mientras Jesús todavía hablaba, llegaron algunos de la casa del jefe de la sinagoga. «Tu hija ha muerto —le dijeron—. ¿Para qué molestar más al Maestro?».
es.R: Jesús todavía estaba hablando cuando llegaron unas personas de la casa de Jairo. Le dijeron a Jairo: «Tu hija ya murió. No hagas venir al Maestro ahora».

sw.L: Alipokuwa bado akisema, wanakuja [watu] kutoka [nyumbani kwa] mkuu wa sinagogi, wakisema, "Binti yako amekufa; kwa nini unaendelea kumsumbua Mwalimu?"
sw.B: Yesu alipokuwa bado akizungumza, watu walifika kutoka nyumbani kwa kiongozi wa sinagogi, wakasema, "Binti yako amekufa. Hakuna haja ya kumsumbua Mwalimu tena."
sw.R: Yesu alipokuwa bado akiongea, watu fulani walifika kutoka nyumbani kwa Yairo. Walimwambia Yairo, "Binti yako amekwisha kufa. Usimsumbue Mwalimu aje sasa."

decisions.choice: from the synagogue leader: from his house
decisions.reason: Jairus is with Jesus, so the messengers come from his household.

decisions.choice: why trouble the teacher any longer: it is too late
decisions.reason: The question means there is no point now. They expect nothing more.

decisions.choice: they come: the present tense of storytelling
decisions.reason: As elsewhere in the chapter.

decisions.choice: They said to Jairus
decisions.reason: Readable names the one they speak to.

source.text: ὁ δὲ Ἰησοῦς παρακούσας τὸν λόγον λαλούμενον λέγει τῷ ἀρχισυναγώγῳ· Μὴ φοβοῦ, μόνον πίστευε.

records.literal_gloss: The but Jesus, having overheard the word being spoken, says to the synagogue leader, Not fear, only believe.

en.L: But Jesus, overhearing the word being spoken, says to the synagogue leader, "Do not fear, only believe."
en.B: But Jesus paid no attention to what they said and told the synagogue leader, "Do not be afraid. Just believe."
